clue.text: Drink stirred up, taste is drawing chap in

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters are jumbled into a new order
to draw something in is to pull it inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: Someone stirs a drink and finds that the flavour pulls a man in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirred up' reads as one phrase, but only 'stirred' is the signal; 'up' is part of the fodder with 'taste is', and the chap is placed inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti spumante is a sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont, so it is a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Judge runs into a vicious dog, perhaps?

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a vicious dog is one example of something that bites

explanation.surface: A judge somehow ends up running into a savage dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The R goes between A and BITER; 'perhaps' warns that a vicious dog is only one example of a biter.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is a person who settles disputes and gives rulings, which is what a judge does.

clue.text: Mark placed over letter, line in ebbing and flowing waves

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: L is a standard abbreviation for line
the sea's rise and fall, ebbing and flowing

explanation.surface: Someone describes a squiggly mark drawn like a line of rising and falling waves.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nicely describes the wavy shape of the mark itself; the L sits inside TIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilde is the small wavy accent written above a letter, as on the Spanish ñ.

clue.text: Rough estimates, most arousing

indicators.note: something rough is crude and unpolished, so the letters come out in a disordered arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A list of rough estimates is being ranked by which is the most exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough estimates' looks like a ballpark figure, but 'Rough' is the signal and 'estimates' supplies exactly the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy is an informal word for erotic or sexy, so the steamiest scene is the most sexually exciting one.

clue.text: Some digit I nudged up, whole number

indicators.note: 'some' means only a portion, so the letters are a run taken from inside the words
in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: Someone nudges a figure upwards to arrive at a round number.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'digIT I NUdged' and read upwards in the grid, which is why 'up' signals the reversal in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is the number one, the smallest positive integer, so it is an example of a whole number.

clue.text: A horse drives characters mixed up with those?

blocks.note: taken as written
a nag is an old or worn-out horse
to drive something in hard is to ram it

explanation.surface: A horse is driving a cart of scrambled letters, as if delivering the type.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is self-referential: the question mark marks a playful description of the very device crosswords use, letters jumbled to make new words.
explanation.definitionFit: Anagrams are words formed by rearranging the letters of other words, so their letters have been scrambled.

clue.text: Musical instruction that unites those twenty instruments, first of all

indicators.note: taking the first of all of a group of words means using only the opening letter of each

blocks.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A score marking tells all twenty players in the orchestra to come together.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay also nearly defines the answer: an instruction uniting all the instruments is exactly what this direction means.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is Italian for 'all', a direction in a score telling every performer in the ensemble to play together.

clue.text: Ironing needing immediate attention

blocks.note: first meaning: smoothing clothes with a hot iron
second meaning: urgent

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a pile of laundry that cannot wait; the two halves are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the act of flattening clothes with heat and an adjective meaning urgent, demanding quick action.

clue.text: Commanding figure, champion boxer, say?

blocks.note: the champion is at the top
a boxer is a breed of dog; 'say' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A heavyweight boxing champion is pictured as the most dominant person around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' wants to be a fighter, but here it is the German breed of dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Top dog is an idiom for the person in charge, the one holding most power in a group.

clue.text: Extravagant player in a female performer

blocks.note: slang for a flashy, big-spending sports star
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A flamboyant actor is cast opposite a woman on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal, but it is simply two letters in the charade; 'baller' is modern slang for a rich, showy athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina is a woman who dances in ballet, so she is a female stage artiste.

clue.text: Rock like that in chest

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor
'so' means in that way

explanation.surface: Someone wants a stone like that one to put inside a treasure chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chest' suggests a box for treasure; it is the body part. A tor is a craggy outcrop on English moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, which includes the upper front region around the ribs.

clue.text: Girl playing Hamlet

indicators.note: playing with something means toying with it, so the letters are moved around

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman is cast in the title role of Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' looks like acting a part, but it signals that the letters of Hamlet are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelma is a female first name, and crosswords routinely clue any woman's name as a girl.

clue.text: Power in a stride that’s extraordinary, proceeded on foot

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the ordinary, so its letters leave their usual order
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: taken as written
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A walker with a remarkably powerful stride marches onward.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'a stride' are rearranged first, and then P is placed inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk wearily or reluctantly, so traipsed means went somewhere by walking.

clue.text: Swine more foolish?

definitions.note: the answer comes from a swine rather than meaning one; the question mark admits the stretch

blocks.note: first meaning: a slice of bacon, cut from a pig
second meaning: more reckless, comparative of a word for hasty

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as calling someone a pig and an idiot; in fact one meaning is a strip of pork and the other a comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of bacon is cut from a pig, and the comparative of an adjective meaning reckless means acting with less sense.

clue.text: Melon is a funny food for puddings

indicators.note: something funny is odd or peculiar, so the letters fall into a strange new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that melon is an odd choice for a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like the link to the definition, but it belongs to the eight letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina is coarse durum wheat flour, cooked with milk into a traditional British milk pudding.

clue.text: Fabulous overhead skill?

definitions.note: the answer is the shot's verbal noun; the question mark admits the cryptic angle

blocks.note: first meaning: excellent, a British informal word of praise
second meaning: hitting the ball hard downward from above the head in tennis

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like praise for a trick shot; in tennis and badminton a smash is a powerful overhead stroke, and the word is also British slang for wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a British informal term of praise meaning terrific, and also the act of playing powerful overhead tennis strokes.

clue.text: Plain site, green building

indicators.note: building means constructing, so the letters are assembled into something new

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A simple building plot, with an eco-friendly construction on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' reads as an adjective, simple, but it is the noun: a wide flat grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a vast savanna grassland in Tanzania, famous for wildlife migrations, so it is a plain.

clue.text: Speak to jerks after wife, showing chink in armour

indicators.note: a jerk is a sudden jolt, and jolting things knocks the letters out of order

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to talk to the idiots who come after a spouse, revealing a vulnerability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerks' looks like a noun for fools; it is a verb signalling the letters are jolted about. 'After' places the scrambled letters after W.
explanation.definitionFit: A chink in someone's armour is an idiom for a vulnerability, a place where they can be attacked.

clue.text: Care shown welcoming ’em, serve tea

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: taking care or trouble over something is bothering
the shortened 'them', with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A host takes trouble to welcome guests and pour them a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll be mother' is a British phrase said by whoever offers to pour the tea for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage the idiom means to take on the job of pouring out the tea for a group.

clue.text: What is secured by strap at the back

indicators.note: whatever is secured by something is held fast inside it, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: to strap something is to bind it
'eh?' is a request to repeat, like 'what?'

explanation.surface: A riddle asks what a strap holds in place on the rear of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What' looks like the start of a question, but it is the interjection a listener uses to ask you to repeat yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind is an adverb or preposition meaning in the rear position, so it means located to the rear.

clue.text: Shock when leader of republic enters battle

indicators.note: the leader goes in front, so only the opening letter is wanted
entering something means going inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
a battle is a fight

explanation.surface: There is consternation when a nation's president joins a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of republic' sounds like a president, but it just means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fright is a sudden feeling of fear, which is what a shock produces, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Winding force in trio son composed

indicators.note: to compose is to arrange or put together, so the letters are set in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A son writes a winding, forceful piece for a chamber trio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' suggests music writing alongside 'trio', but it signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Torsion is the twisting of an object by opposed turning forces, as in a twisted spring or rod.

clue.text: Capital that man links, strangely, with capital in Iceland

indicators.note: something done strangely is done in an odd way, so the letters come out in an unusual order
a capital letter starts a proper name, so only the opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: 'that man' is he
taken as written
the opening letter of the country

explanation.surface: A man oddly connects one Nordic capital city with Reykjavik.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'capital' wants to be Reykjavik; it means the capital letter of Iceland.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital city of Finland, the seat of its government, so it is a capital.

clue.text: Inappropriate forty winks in it

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the first letter of the word, opened up
forty winks is a short sleep
the last letter of the same word

explanation.surface: Someone frowns on dozing off in the middle of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The short sleep sits inside the two-letter word IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or not fitting the occasion, which is a synonym for unbecoming or improper.

clue.text: Cruel blocking off entrance to theme park?

indicators.note: blocking off an entrance closes the way in, so the opening letter is removed

blocks.note: a theme park is a kind of fairground, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Barring the gates of an amusement park strikes someone as heartless.
explanation.walkthrough: FUNFAIR loses its first letter; the question mark admits that a theme park is only loosely a funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair treatment is unjust and harsh, so the word works as a near-synonym for heartless or unkind.

clue.text: Perfect oil stirred in garlic dip

indicators.note: stirring mixes things around, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook stirs oil into a garlicky sauce until it is just right.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means excellent, and the digit 1 stands in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a Provençal sauce of garlic emulsified with olive oil, often served for dipping.

clue.text: Work on painting initially, American

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the opening letters are taken

blocks.note: the opening letters of these two words
US is short for the United States, hence American

explanation.surface: An American artist gets to work on a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work on' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'Work' alone is the definition and 'on' joins the selected words.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is Latin for a creative work, used especially for numbered musical compositions.

clue.text: New girl, old relative

blocks.note: N is the standard abbreviation for new
Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A family has a newborn daughter and an elderly kinswoman.
explanation.walkthrough: Nanna is a British informal word for grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanna is a grandmother, an older family member of a generation two steps above.

clue.text: Slices of meat, vegetable upon one

blocks.note: a pepper is a vegetable
upon means on
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pizza topping of meat slices with a vegetable on top of each.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a pizza, and the answer is its classic topping.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy cured sausage usually served thinly cut, as on a pizza, so it is sliced meat.

clue.text: It’s titanic, as complicated for data analyst

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled and intricate, so the letters are muddled up

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A huge dataset seems enormously complicated to the person crunching the numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Titanic' suggests a ship or something huge, but it only lends its letters to the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A statistician collects and interprets numerical information, so the job is analysing figures.
